title: POLICE: Man wounded in shoulder during Kathleen Street traffic stop
article: Greater Sudbury Police and the Special Investigations Unit are not saying much about a Monday evening traffic stop that resulted in an officer shooting a 34-year-old man.
At approximately 11 a.m., an officer stopped a vehicle in the Kathleen Street area.
A release issued by the SIU says there was "an interaction" between the driver of the car and the police officer, but doesn't go into detail.
As a result, the officer shot the man, who was arrested and taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.
An SIU official told CBC Radio the man was shot in the shoulder.
Five investigators and two forensic investigators are looking into what happened.
Since 2010, the Greater Sudbury Police Service has been investigated five times by the SIU, including Monday's incident.
On Dec. 29, 2010, the investigating body got involved to check into the circumstances surrounding another man who was shot.
Two officers went to a residence on Pine Street after getting reports that 46-year-old Marcel Tranchemontagne had stabbed his roommate.
When they arrived, Tranchemontagne was on the phone with 911 and had a knife in his hand, which he refused to put down.
Ignoring commands from the officers to drop the knife, both of them shot him.
He was taken to hospital and died.
Ian Scott, the director of the SIU, cleared both officers in that instance, saying they were in the right to use lethal force, as it appeared the man posed a real threat to their safety.
Other investigations have been for a man who sustained injuries while at a bush party and a man who got into a car accident while trying to evade police.
